title: The acyclic matching conjecture with unit acyclicity sequence
literal_statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $A,B\subseteq G$ be finite subsets with $A\cap(A+B)=\emptyset$. Write $\mathcal{M}(A,B)$ for the set of matchings from $A$ to $B$. An acyclicity sequence records the multiplicities of the support of a matching in non-increasing order. **Unit acyclicity-sequence conjecture.** There exists $f\in\mathcal{M}(A,B)$ such that $f$ is acyclic and its acyclicity sequence contains only $1$. The conjecture is motivated by simulation results and is intended as a constructive approach to the weak acyclic matching property; it remains open in the source.

source.note: Exact admissible coset pair in ZMod3 times ZMod2; every unit multiplicity matching has a distinct output-translate with identical labelled multiplicity.
